newsitem.title: USA: Manitoba electric lines seen up early next week.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba electric lines seen up early next week.

text.p: Two major power transmission lines in northern Manitoba owned by Manitoba Hydro will likely be partially restored early next week after being knocked out by a storm Thursday, a company spokesman said.
The two lines move about 3,000 megawatts (MW) of power south from hydroelectric facilities in northern Manitoba.
An average of about 1,500 MW of Manitoba Hydro power is exported to Minnesota and North Dakota this time of year.
"We hope to have a temporary situation in place early next week," said Manitoba Hydro spokesman Glenn Schneider, adding this would enable transmitting almost the full 3,000 MW.
"In the meantime we've dropped our exports and asked our neighboring utilities to help out," Schneider said.
Because the company has been able to purchase power from outside the province and demand is average, the spokesman said the utility should not have to cut electricity supply.
Transmission lines out of Manitoba have been reversed, so the province is now importing about 800 MW from the U.S.
The reversal of the line boosted power prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) and Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) regions, traders and brokers said.
Power in both MAIN and MAPP was said to be trading near $19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for weekend delivery and near $25.00 for Monday, sources said.
Next-day power was said to have jumped to as high as $45.00 on Thursday after the line reversal was announced.
Next-day power in the regions was trading at $17.00-19.00 last week.
The two Manitoba Hydro lines were knocked out when several towers toppled during high storm winds, Schneider said.
Manitoba Hydro is a government owned utility with a total generation capacity of 5,200 MW, about 98 percent of which comes from hydroelectric facilities.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
